newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NatMut may spend A$40 mln on China.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NatMut may spend A$40 mln on China.

text.p: Australian life insurer National Mutual Holdings Ltd is likely to spend A$40 million to establish an operation in China if it wins approval from Beijing, managing director Geoff Tomlinson said on Thursday.
National Mutual has applied for insurance licences to operate in Shanghai and Guongdong province and says China's emerging middle class represents a key, long term market.
Tomlinson said the company had used a computer model to make conservative projections of the start-up costs and profitability, assuming it operates initially in Shanghai.

"It basically shows what I consider to be conservative assumptions," he told Reuters said after addressing a business lunch in Melbourne. "We would invest A$40 million into the business and reach capital self-sufficiency and start turning a profit by the end of the fourth year."
Tomlinson said he did not expect Beijing to decide the fate of National Mutual's application any time soon, after Prime Minister John Howard's visit to China in late March.
"I am personally very much in favour of the prime minister's visit, but in terms of National Mutual I do not expect any short-term benefit for National Mutual out of the visit."
